cells.title: Rome founded
cells.detail:
Rome founded

According to legend, Romulus founded the city on the Palatine Hill after killing his twin brother Remus.

cells.title: Republic begins
cells.detail:
The Republic begins

The last king, Tarquin the Proud, is expelled and power passes to two elected consuls.

cells.title: Battle of Marathon
cells.detail:
Battle of Marathon

Athens defeats the first Persian invasion of Greece.

cells.title: First Punic War
cells.detail:
First Punic War

Rome and Carthage fight over Sicily. Rome builds its first large navy to win.

cells.title: War with Rome
cells.detail:
War with Rome

Carthage, the leading naval power of the western Mediterranean, is dragged into war over Sicily.

cells.title: Cannae
cells.detail:
Battle of Cannae

Hannibal encircles and destroys a much larger Roman army in southern Italy.

global.title: Carthage and Corinth destroyed
global.detail:
Carthage and Corinth destroyed

Rome razes Carthage at the end of the Third Punic War and crushes the Achaean League in Greece, becoming master of the Mediterranean.

cells.title: Crossing the Rubicon
cells.detail:
Crossing the Rubicon

Julius Caesar leads his army across the Rubicon into Italy, starting a civil war.

cells.title: Caesar assassinated
cells.detail:
The Ides of March

Caesar is stabbed by a group of senators led by Brutus and Cassius.

cells.title: Battle of Actium
cells.detail:
Battle of Actium

Octavian's fleet defeats Antony and Cleopatra off the coast of Greece.

global.title: Augustus becomes emperor
global.detail:
Augustus becomes emperor

Octavian receives the title Augustus, ending the Republic and starting the Roman Empire.

global.title: Pax Romana
global.detail:
Pax Romana

About two centuries of relative peace and stability across the empire begin.

cells.title: Colosseum opens
cells.detail:
The Colosseum

Opened under Titus with 100 days of games.

cells.title: Maximum extent
cells.detail:
Maximum extent

Under Trajan the empire reaches its largest size.

cells.title: Empire splits
cells.detail:
The empire splits

After the death of Theodosius I the empire is divided for good. The eastern half, where Greek dominates, becomes the Byzantine Empire.

cells.title: Western Empire falls
cells.detail:
Fall of the Western Empire

Odoacer deposes the last western emperor, Romulus Augustulus.

cells.title: Constantinople falls
cells.detail:
Fall of Constantinople

The Ottomans under Mehmed II take the city, ending the Eastern Roman Empire.
